chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever seeks hadith for the benefit of this world, there will be no share for him in the Hereafter; and whoever seeks it for the goodness of the Hereafter, God will give him the goodness of this world and the Hereafter.

key_terms.الحديث: hadith — prophetic narrations and reports; here referring to the act of seeking and transmitting religious knowledge
key_terms.خير الآخرة: goodness of the Hereafter — spiritual reward and salvation in the next life
key_terms.منفعة الدنيا: benefit of this world — worldly gain, social status, or material reward
key_terms.نصيب: share/portion — one's allotted portion in the Hereafter's rewards

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the intention behind seeking hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against the corruption of intention in seeking religious knowledge. In the intellectual culture of early Islam, the transmission of hadith was both a spiritual act and a means to social prestige or livelihood. This teaching emphasizes that the purity of one's intention (niyyah) determines spiritual reward: seeking hadith for worldly gain forfeits the afterlife, while seeking it for the sake of the Hereafter earns both worldly and eternal blessings.
